title: Review: the edge-case habit
idea: Pull the unit together: spot empty/zero/impossible cases, guard the divisor, and handle the edge before the normal work. Mostly thinking.

exercises.prompt: The question to ask for EVERY problem is...
options: What if there's nothing, or it's zero?
exercises.explanation: That one question surfaces most edge cases. It is the habit this whole unit built.

exercises.prompt: Which computation can crash on a bad value?
exercises.explanation: Division by a zero count crashes. Addition and multiplication are always safe.

exercises.prompt: A guard is just an if/else aimed at the edge case - no new syntax.
exercises.explanation: Right. You already know if/else; a guard is simply using it to handle the empty/zero/impossible case.

exercises.prompt: Match each problem to its edge case.
exercises.explanation: Division fears a zero divisor; 'first of' fears empty; accepting input fears impossible values.
count is 0, so the guard fires: No data. The risky step is skipped.

exercises.prompt: Order the safe shape for any edge-case problem.
blocks: If it is the edge case, handle it specially
exercises.explanation: Edge case first, normal work in the else. The same shape fits every guarded problem.

exercises.prompt: Which value is NOT usually an edge case?
exercises.explanation: A normal middle value is the easy case. Zero, empty, and impossible values are the edges.

exercises.prompt: Some problems need no guard at all.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Pure addition or multiplication is always safe. Guard only where a bad value is actually possible.
stock is 0, so the guard reports Sold out - a clear message for the empty case.

exercises.prompt: After this unit, the skill you carry forward is...
options: Spotting and guarding the empty/zero/impossible case
exercises.explanation: Spot the edge case and guard it. Next, elif will let one decision sort into many outcomes.
